result.rationale: The diff shows refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set (returns `response` from fetch), while the Google CalendarService code does `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` — a fetch Response has no `.data` property, so token is undefined and token.access_token throws. This is a real defect introduced by this diff.

judged_text: In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but this code reads res?.data — the Gaxios response shape produced by myGoogleAuth.refreshToken — so token is undefined. With CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, every expired-token refresh for google calendar throws a TypeError at token.access_token ('Cannot read properties of undefined'), so the integration fails on each use whose access token has expired; the sync feature simply does not work for google calendar.

record.issue_text: [BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but this code reads res?.data — the Gaxios response shape produced by myGoogleAuth.refreshToken — so token is undefined. With CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, every expired-token refresh for google calendar throws a TypeError at token.access_token ('Cannot read properties of undefined'), so the integration fails on each use whose access token has expired; the sync feature simply does not work for google calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, the code assigns `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then reads `const token = res?.data` (expecting the Gaxios `{ data: ... }` shape returned by `myGoogleAuth.refreshToken(...).res`). But `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch(...)` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`), and a `Response` has no `.data` property. In sync mode this makes `token` undefined and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime, breaking Google Calendar token refresh.
